title: Slano, Croatia 2027: First-Time Visitor Guide & Tips
metaDescription: Plan a first trip to Slano, Croatia: how to get there, best beaches, where to eat, day trips to Ston, Trsteno and Mljet, costs in euros and local tips.
content:
## Where Is Slano and Who Is It For?

Slano is a village in Dubrovnik-Neretva County, set on a bay about 2 km long. It lies on the coast road between Dubrovnik and Ston, roughly 34 km northwest of Dubrovnik and 60 km from Dubrovnik Airport. The village has a few restaurants, small shops, a harbour, two larger hotels and many private apartments. There is no nightlife district.

Slano suits families, couples, divers, cyclists and anyone using it as a cheaper, calmer base for the Dubrovnik area. Visitors who want bars, boutiques and a busy promenade will find it too quiet.

## How to Get to Slano

### By car
The drive from Dubrovnik takes 40-45 minutes along the D8 coastal road. From Dubrovnik Airport allow about 1 hour. From Split it is roughly 210 km. From Zagreb it is about 465 km. The Split route passes through a short stretch of Bosnia and Herzegovina at Neum unless you take the Pelješac Bridge route, which stays in Croatia. Carry passports or ID for the Neum crossing.

### By bus
Regional buses run from Dubrovnik bus station to Slano, taking about 45 minutes. Buses stop in the village centre near the harbour. Fares are in the single-digit euro range each way. Frequency drops sharply on Sundays and in the off-season, so check the current timetable at the station on arrival. Buses between Dubrovnik and Split or Zagreb also stop in Slano, but check each service first.

### Airport transfer
Private transfers from the airport cost roughly €80-100. Ask your host to arrange one, as hosts often quote less than taxi apps. Rental cars at the airport are the most flexible option for a stay of more than three days.

## Best Time to Visit Slano

- **June and September:** Sea temperatures are comfortable, roads are clearer and accommodation costs less than in July and August.
- **July and August:** Hot and busy by local standards. Book accommodation well ahead. The village stays far less crowded than Dubrovnik.
- **May and October:** Good for hiking and cycling. Some seasonal restaurants and cafés may be closed.
- **November to March:** Many tourist businesses close. Visit only if you want complete quiet.

## Beaches in Slano

Slano's beaches are mostly pebble, with some stone and paved sections. Sand is limited.

- **Sv. Jeronim:** A beach about 150 m long beside the port. It has showers, loungers and cafés, and is the easiest choice if you are staying in the centre.
- **Banja:** A quieter pebble beach a short walk or drive from the centre.
- **Osmine and Grgurići:** Smaller bays outside the centre, good for calmer swimming away from the harbour.
- **Karmelska:** Has toilets, showers, parking and sports fields, which suits families.

The bay is sheltered, so the water is usually calm. It works well for kayaking, snorkelling and diving. Bring water shoes, since the pebbles and sea urchins make entry uncomfortable in some spots.

The beaches are pleasant but not dramatic. Adults who want a long beach day with plenty of variety may find them repetitive after three or four days. Plan boat or day trips rather than treating Slano as a pure beach stay.

## What to See in and Around Slano

### In the village
Slano has a few historic buildings from the time of the Dubrovnik Republic. These include the Rector's Palace, the Franciscan monastery and summer houses built by Dubrovnik noble families. The village is compact and takes about an hour to walk through, including the waterfront.

### Ston and Mali Ston
Stons's defensive wall is about 5.5 km long, among the longest in Europe. It climbs steeply from the town, so go early in summer. Mali Ston, a short drive away, is known for oysters and mussels farmed in the bay. Ston also has historic salt pans. Allow half a day. A dozen oysters at a Mali Ston restaurant usually costs around €15-25.

### Trsteno Arboretum
Trsteno, on the way to Dubrovnik, has a 15th-century arboretum with old plane trees and a Renaissance garden. Allow about 1.5 hours.

### Dubrovnik
Dubrovnik Old Town is a day trip of 40-45 minutes each way. Go in the morning, walk the city walls first, and be back on the road before the evening rush. The roads out of the city slow down between 17:00 and 19:00 in summer.

### Mljet and the Elaphiti Islands
Ferries to Mljet leave from Prapratno, near Ston, about 30 minutes from Slano. Mljet National Park has two saltwater lakes and is worth a full day. Boat operators in Slano also rent small motor and sail boats for exploring nearby islands. The Elaphiti Islands are reached more easily by ferry from Dubrovnik.

## Where to Eat in Slano

The waterfront has several family-run restaurants and cafés. Konoba Kolarin, opposite the port, is a family-run restaurant and hotel that serves local specialities. Grgurici and Maestral are also local options. Mirakul is a beachfront café.

Order the catch of the day, black risotto, octopus salad or grilled fish, and ask for a local wine such as Dingač or Pošip. Expect €12-20 for a main course and €35-60 per kilo for fresh fish. Confirm the weight and total price before the fish is cooked.

Skip the pizza places along the harbour if you want local food, and choose a konoba serving the day's catch instead. Menus there are shorter and more seasonal.

## Where to Stay in Slano

Most visitors stay in private apartments and rooms, usually within 10 minutes' walk of the harbour. Slano also has hotels, including Admiral and Osmine, which have restaurants, pools and sports facilities. Campsites are available just outside the village.

Typical summer prices:

- Apartments: €50-110 per night for two people
- Private rooms: €40-80 per night
- Hotels: €100-200 per night in peak season
- Campsites: about €18-30 per night for a pitch with a small family

Off-season rates are often 30-40% lower. Choose accommodation close to the harbour if you do not have a car, because walking from outer areas can take 30-40 minutes.

## Local Tips for First-Time Visitors

- **Bring cash.** Smaller konobas, beach cafés and parking attendants may not take cards.
- **Shop early.** Supermarkets and bakeries open early and many close by evening. Sunday hours are shorter.
- **Rent a car for the region.** Bus services between villages are thin. A car costs about €40-80 per day in season and gives access to Ston, Mljet and Trsteno.
- **Avoid driving into Dubrovnik Old Town.** Parking is expensive and limited. Park at a garage outside the walls or use the bus.
- **Use the Pelješac Bridge.** If you are heading to Korčula or Orebić, the route from Slano is straightforward and avoids the border queue at Neum.
- **Check ferry timetables.** Mljet ferries run on seasonal schedules and fill up in July and August.
- **Walk the old trails.** Marked paths run through olive groves, pines and orchards. Bring water and a hat, since shade is limited in summer.

## Is Slano Worth Visiting?

Slano is worth visiting for a quiet base, lower prices and access to Ston, Mljet and Dubrovnik. It is not worth visiting if you want nightlife, large beaches or a full programme of entertainment. Stay two to five nights, use it as a base for day trips, and book accommodation early for July and August.

faq.question: How far is Slano from Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Slano is about 34 km from Dubrovnik, a drive of 40-45 minutes along the D8 coastal road. Regional buses take about 45 minutes. Dubrovnik Airport is roughly 60 km away, about 1 hour by car.

faq.question: Is Slano a good place for a family holiday?
faq.answer: Yes. The bay is sheltered, the water is calm and several beaches have showers and loungers. Karmelska has sports fields and parking. The village is quiet and has no late-night scene.

faq.question: Does Slano have sandy beaches?
faq.answer: Slano's beaches are mostly pebble, with some stone and paved areas and only small stretches of sand. Sv. Jeronim by the harbour is the most convenient. Water shoes are useful.

faq.question: How do I get from Dubrovnik to Slano without a car?
faq.answer: Take a regional or long-distance bus from Dubrovnik bus station. The trip takes about 45 minutes and the bus stops in the village centre. Service is limited on Sundays and in winter, so check the timetable first.

faq.question: What are the best day trips from Slano?
faq.answer: Ston and Mali Ston (about 17 km) offer the long walls and oysters. Trsteno Arboretum and Dubrovnik lie to the southeast. Mljet National Park is reached by ferry from Prapratno, about 30 minutes away.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Slano?
faq.answer: June and September are the best months, with warm sea, fewer people and lower prices than July and August. May and October suit hiking, but some businesses are closed. Most tourist services close from November to March.

faq.question: How much does a trip to Slano cost?
faq.answer: Apartments cost roughly €50-110 per night in summer and rooms €40-80. A restaurant main course is around €12-20. A car rental adds about €40-80 per day in season.

quickAnswer: Slano is a quiet fishing village on the Dubrovnik Riviera, about 34 km northwest of Dubrovnik (40 minutes by car). It suits visitors who want calm pebble beaches, family-run restaurants and cheaper stays. Use a car or the Dubrovnik bus, and plan day trips to Ston, Trsteno and Mljet.
